title: Tesserae device manifest
description: Shape of device.json. A device is the consumer side of one or more renderers: it subscribes to a status heartbeat topic, optionally publishes to a config topic, and (informationally) lists which renderers it can ingest.

icon.description: Phosphor icon slug (no 'ph-' prefix) shown in device pickers and the settings card. Instances may override the kind's default.

renderers.description: Renderer ids this device consumes. Informational for the UI; renderers run regardless of which devices are loaded.

status_topic.description: MQTT topic the device publishes its heartbeat to. Tesserae subscribes and parses payloads through device.parse_status(). Omit for devices that don't use MQTT for status (e.g. HTTP-polled clients like TRMNL, their status comes from request headers, parsed by app/trmnl_api.py).

config_topic.description: MQTT topic for outbound config. Omit if the device has no configurable knobs OR pushes config through a non-MQTT channel (TRMNL embeds refresh_rate in /api/display responses, not over MQTT).

config_schema.description: Field definitions for the config form. Each value is a {type, default, min?, max?, label?, choices?} dict.

integration.description: For 'ha_device_picker': the Home Assistant integration domain whose devices populate the dropdown (e.g. 'opendisplay').

presets.description: For numeric fields: a set of named preset values shown in a dropdown alongside a 'Custom…' option that reveals a number input. Submitted value is whichever the user landed on.

retired.description: A setting that newer behaviour replaced. The device page shows the field only while a device still holds a value other than its default, so the operator can clear it; once cleared it is gone, and new devices never see it. The stored value is still honoured.

group.description: Name of a group on the device page to put this field in (e.g. 'Power'); fields sharing a name sit together under it, after Rendering. Absent: the field stays in Identity, Rendering or Timing by its type. 'sign' and 'sign_net' are reserved for Visionect's frame settings.

show_if.description: Show this field only while other fields of the kind hold these values, e.g. {"power_control": "switch"}. Same grammar as a widget option's show_if (a value, a list of values, or {"not": ...}). The field is hidden, not removed, so its value is still saved.

panel.description: Physical panel attached to this device. Multi-head installs use this to size each device's compositions independently; pages can be assigned to a specific device and inherit its panel.

orientation.description: How the user wants to read the dashboard. Landscape/portrait sets the canvas aspect; the '_flipped' variants add a 180° turn the renderer applies for an upside-down physical mount. The renderer already maps the composition onto its client's fixed buffer direction.

name.description: Friendly name shown in the UI.

touch.description: Whether this kind's panel takes taps Tesserae dispatches. Absent → display-only.

buttons.description: Whether this kind can send Tesserae button presses. Set false for a device with no physical buttons (or whose protocol forwards none): its device page shows no button map and Home Assistant gets no Input event entity for it. Absent → it may have buttons.

battery.description: Whether this kind runs on a battery. Set false for a mains-powered display (a TV, say): its device page shows no Power section. Absent → it may have one.

palettes.description: Colour palettes (panel gamuts) the operator may pick for a device of this kind, for hardware that comes in several and cannot report which it has (an OpenDisplay tag is sold as black and white, red, red and yellow, six-colour or grey). The device page then shows a Colour palette choice in Panel, stored as panel.gamut. Absent → the kind's own panel.gamut is fixed.

renderer_settings.description: Whether the per-device settings of this kind's renderer (client rotation, scale, letterbox colour) apply. Set false for a kind whose publisher sends the composition itself rather than the renderer's output: its device page leaves them out. Absent → they apply.

locale.description: locale this device renders widget panel text in (e.g. 'fr', 'pt-BR'). An instance overrides its kind's value if the kind declares one; absent at both levels falls back to the app-wide default (settings.app.locale). Lets one server drive a German kitchen panel and an English office panel with the same widgets. See app/locale_resolve.py.
